ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a cyclobutyl skeleton; the right side of the ring is connected through a methylene to a terminal NH2, namely cyclobutylmethyl amine (cyclobutyl-CH2-NH2). A lone pair of electrons is marked beside the nitrogen of NH2; a curved arrow points from this lone pair to the nitrogen atom in the N/O fragment on the right. Another curved arrow is also drawn inside the right-side N/O unit, indicating that this fragment undergoes electron rearrangement. Reasoning: According to the arrow pushing, the lone pair of the amine nitrogen forms a new N–N bond with the right-side nitrogen atom, while electron rearrangement within the N/O fragment gives a nitroso form. The product connectivity is O=N–N–CH2–cyclobutyl, corresponding to the SMILES O=NNCC1CCC1.

method.method_draft: 1) Inspect the image and identify the substrate as cyclobutyl-CH2-CH2-NH2. 2) Follow the curved arrow from the amine lone pair to the electrophilic nitrogen on the right-hand N/O fragment. 3) Apply the second arrow inside the N/O unit to complete the electron relocation and stabilize the product. 4) Write the product connectivity with the amine nitrogen now incorporated into the nitroso linkage, giving O=NNCC1CCC1.
